title: 10 Largemouth Bass Facts in Under 30 Seconds
hook: Ten largemouth facts in under thirty seconds.
script: Ten largemouth facts in under thirty seconds. Its upper jaw reaches past its eye. Fry eat zooplankton, then hunt at about two inches. One female can lay up to 43,000 eggs. Dad chases her off and guards the eggs. He fans out the nest with his tail. Bigger bass will eat the smaller ones. They're most voracious in low light. They can't burp gas from their swim bladder. Native east of the Rockies, now introduced worldwide. The record: 22 pounds 4 ounces, 1932. Which one did you already know?

question: Which one did you already know?

claims.text: A largemouth bass's upper jaw reaches past the rear of its eye.
Largemouth fry eat zooplankton and become active predators at about two inches.
A female largemouth lays roughly 2,000 to 43,000 eggs in a nest.
The male chases the female away and guards the eggs.
Male largemouth fan out the nest with their tails.
Larger largemouth bass prey on smaller bass.
Largemouth bass are especially voracious in low light.
Bass have no physical outlet to vent swim bladder gas.
Largemouth bass are native east of the Rockies.
Largemouth bass have been introduced to many areas worldwide.
The all-tackle record largemouth, 22 lb 4 oz, was caught by George Perry in 1932 and tied in 2009.
The record weight is 22 lb 4 oz.
